topic: Practical Applications of Visible Light, Ultraviolet, and X-rays
key_concepts: LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.
Lasers produce highly directional, intensified light used in surgery and fiber-optic commu
Optical fibers transmit light by total internal reflection.
An optical fiber has a pure glass core protected by less optically dense cladding.
Optical fibers are used in telecommunications, medical imaging, and weld inspection.
UV radiation comes naturally from the Sun and artificially from UV lamps.
UV light reveals fluorescent security marks and helps identify counterfeit banknotes.
UV radiation sterilizes water and medical equipment by killing bacteria and viruses.
UV exposure helps produce vitamin D but too much can damage skin and eyes.
X-rays are produced when fast-moving electrons hit a metal target in an X-ray tube.
X-rays are used in medical imaging, airport luggage inspection, and industrial crack detec
